nodes.name: One-step supersaturated co-precipitation of a-RNMO
nodes.procedure: 20 ml of aqueous NiCl2·6H20 solution (1 M) was prepared. 20 ml of aqueous Na2MoO4 solution (1 M) containing RuCl3 was rapidly added to the Ni solution under ultrasonic conditions at room temperature. Precipitates were formed immediately. After 10 min of ultrasonic vibration, the precipitates were collected by centrifugation and washed with water and ethanol three times, then dried.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal and Annealing for c-NMO
nodes.procedure: 0.349 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.371 g (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O were dissolved in 30 ml DI water. pH was adjusted to 7.0 using ammonium hydroxide. The mixture was hydrothermal treated at 150 °C for 6 h. The precipitate was centrifugation, washed, dried at 70 °C, and then annealed in air at 450 °C for 3 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms the amorphous nature of a-NMO and a-RNMO by the absence of diffraction peaks, whereas c-NMO shows strong characteristic peaks of crystalline NiMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Fig. 1b) showed the absence of a crystalline phase in a-NMO and a-RNMO, which was distinct from crystalline NiMoO4 (c-NMO) with strong characteristic peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pair distribution function analysis indicates that a-NMO and a-RNMO are long-range disordered but short-range ordered (correlation ~9 Å) with looser structures and longer M-O bonds (1.90 Å for a-RNMO) compared to c-NMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for the pristine a-NMO and a-RNMO, the crystal structures were long-range disordered but short-range ordered ... amorphous structure had a short-range correlation of about 9 A ... average M–O bond length (1.90 A) was slightly longer than that of a-NMO (1.86 A).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements were used to estimate ECSA, showing a higher specific activity for a-RNMO (0.95 mA cm-2) compared to a-NMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) was estimated from double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements ... a-RNMO presented the highest specific activity (0.95 mA cm-2 ECSA), approximately fourfold than that of a-NMO (0.23 mA cm-2 ECSA).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals that a-RNMO has the lowest charge-transfer resistance (15.33 Ω) among all samples, indicating the fastest charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS Nyquist plots ... a-RNMO showed the smallest Nyquist semicircle and the lowest charge-transfer resistance (Rct) ... Rct of a-RNMO, a-NMO, c-NMO, and RuO2 were 15.33 +/- 0.36 Ohm, 48.82 +/- 0.76 Ohm, 890.70 +/- 9.86 Ohm, and 101.80 +/- 1.18 Ohm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Quick-XAS (2 min resolution) reveals potential-dependent Ni oxidation (Ni K-edge shift of ~2 eV) and structural reconstruction into NiOOH (beta then gamma phases) during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-resolved operando Quick X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals rapid Mo leaching followed by structural reconstruction, culminating in the NiOOH formation ... Ni K-edge continuously shifted toward higher energy by approximately 2 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows rapid Mo dissolution in a-RNMO above 1.30 V and the appearance of NiOOH bending/stretching modes (470, 555 cm^-1) above 1.25 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo–O feature at near 900 cm−1, disappeared in a-RNMO above 1.30 V, suggesting a rapid Mo dissolution ... when the applied potential was above 1.25 V, a-RNMO displayed peaks at 470 cm−1 and 555 cm−1 ... NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms a Ru content of 2.28 at.% and a high Ru/Ni molar ratio (~0.15) for the a-RNMO catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental composition of a-RNMO was analyzed by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) (Supplementary Table 2) ... confirming the Ru content was 2.28 at.%. The molar ratio of Ru to Ni (~0.15) was higher than the theoretical value.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM imaging reveals a-RNMO consists of uniform nanoparticles (~50 nm), while c-NMO consists of short nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a-RNMO exhibited uniform nanoparticle morphology with an average size of about 50 nm ... c‑NMO (Supplementary Fig. 4) consisted of short nanorods

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping and line scanning confirm the uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, O (and Ru in a-RNMO) across the catalyst structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping (Fig. 1h) revealed homogeneous spatial distribution of Ru, Ni, Mo, and O ... Supplementary Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 show the uniform distributions of Ni, Mo, and O elements in a-NMO and c-NMO

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area analysis was used to normalize OER current densities, showing a-RNMO has 10x higher specific activity than a-NMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: OER currents were normalized to the specific Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area (Supplementary Fig. 16). The specific activity of a-RNMO was more than 10 times higher than that of a-NMO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex-situ ICP-MS stability tests indicate negligible Ru and Ni dissolution (<0.25 ppm) but significant Mo leaching during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex-situ ICP-MS test ... dissolution of Ru and Ni was negligible within 100 hours (below 0.25 ppm), while Mo loss was more than ten times to those of Ru and Ni.
